butterflies.question: Do you want a ride that gives you that fluttery, butterfly feeling in your stomach?

system.question: Do you prefer a launch that shoots you forward, or a classic lift hill that takes you up the slope?

exciting.question: Do you enjoy that light butterfly feeling when a ride goes a bit higher or faster?
exciting.yes: Say yes if that excites you.
exciting.no: Say no if you prefer something gentler.

first_coaster.question: Is this your first roller‑coaster adventure?
first_coaster.yes: Say yes if you want to start with something smaller.
first_coaster.no: Say no if you’ve ridden coasters before and feel ready for more.

intense.question: Are you looking for a ride with strong forces and powerful moments?
intense.yes: Say yes if you want a high‑energy experience.
intense.no: Say no if you prefer something more moderate.

inversions.question: Do you enjoy being taken upside‑down in a smooth and controlled way?

comfortable_inversions.question: Do you enjoy coasters that surprise you with unexpected twists and playful misdirection?

spin_wood.question: Do you prefer a spinning coaster or a wooden coaster with a rougher feel?

very_high.question: Are you in the mood for a coaster that’s all about height and a flying sensation?

funny.question: Do you enjoy a light‑hearted ride that’s more about fun than intensity?

indoor.question: Would you like your adventure to take place indoors, surrounded by atmosphere and storytelling?

indoor_type.question: Are you in the mood for a story‑driven dark‑ride adventure, or an indoor coaster with a lively, energetic feel?

rail_type.question: Do you prefer a ride that glides smoothly through wide curves, or one that keeps you alert with quick, surprising turns?

soaked.question: Are you in the mood for a refreshing splash during your ride?

splash_type.question: Do you want a big, dramatic splash at the end of your adventure?

intro.full:
My name is Lars Bakker, and welcome to the Roller Coaster Recommender page. I completed a comprehensive, self-developed IT program. This taught me the basic principles of ethical hacking, advanced mathematics, and web development.

I completed these programs through Harvard CS50, IT Management Group and individual courses from Delft University of Technology EDX. I'm a fan of rollercoasters and Europa Park, so I built a Flask web application that recommends the most suitable Europa Park coaster based on questions about your height and preferences. Europa Park has a total of 14 roller coasters and it's impossible to do them all in one visit, so it's useful to know which ones you shouldn't miss.

Once the questionnaire is completed, the most recommended roller coaster will appear, along with its specifications and a POV onride video. Enjoy! As someone with years of coaster experience, I recommend taking a quick look at the disclaimer. Especially if you're new to roller coasters or recognize yourself in the embedded videos.

Disclaimer.2: This web application is a non_commercial hobby and portfolio project, created for educational purposes and to demonstrate my skills as an aspiring Python and web developer. All rights to any images, videos, or trademarks originating from Europa_Park GmbH en Co. KG remain fully with their respective owners. If Europa_Park or any rights holder requests the removal of specific material, it will be taken down immediately.
Disclaimer.4: Embedded videos remain the property of their respective creators. All YouTube content is sourced from the official channels of the creators listed below:
Disclaimer.5: About the experience ratings of the roller coasters
Disclaimer.6: The coaster experience ratings in this web app are general indicators and can vary significantly from person to person. They are based on the average roller coaster rider and should not be interpreted as medical or professional advice. Individuals with sensitive stomachs, balance issues, heart conditions, or other health concerns should always exercise caution when riding roller coasters.
Disclaimer.7: Your personal experience, comfort level, and riding history also play an important role. For example, an experienced young adult may find Voltron to be an exceptional ride, while a 9 year old on their first roller coaster may find it too intense.
Disclaimer.8: All information provided in this web app is intended solely for educational and entertainment purposes. When visiting Europa_Park, always follow the official safety instructions and signage at each attraction.
Disclaimer.trillvieuw 1: When I was a young kid, roller coasters felt pretty intimidating to me. That’s why I understand exactly how intense it can feel the first time you go upside down, drop from a big height or worry about getting a little nauseous.
Disclaimer.trillvieuw 2: Not all roller coasters at Europa‑Park feel the same. Some are smooth and accessible for almost everyone, while others offer more speed, height or physical force. That doesn’t make them “scary”, but it does mean they can feel more intense, especially for children or visitors who are still new to bigger coasters. The Thrillview helps you understand which rides are a bit stronger and where extra guidance for children can be helpful.
Disclaimer.trillvieuw 3: This includes coasters with a launch, significant height, strong vibrations or spinning cars. This information is meant to give you clarity and confidence before you ride, so you know what to expect and which order makes sense if you’re still building experience. That way, you and your child or group can choose rides that match your comfort level.

RnR.1: My coaster recommender is based on Europa Park, but my history as a roller coaster fan didn't begin in Europa Park. My roller coaster hobby began in Disneyland Paris. My first roller coaster was the Big Thunder Mountain, and my first intense roller coaster was the Rock 'n' Roller Coaster. Where does my roller coaster enthusiasm come from? For that, we have to go back to 2003. I was only nine years old, on vacation in Disneyland Paris with my parents and my brother.
RnR.2:
It was a time before POV videos and modern smartphones. If you were nine years old in 2003, you couldn’t simply look on your own phone or computer to see what attractions to expect at an amusement park.

You certainly wouldn’t know what was inside a building with a huge sign that said “Rock ’n’ Roller Coaster” in bright lights, complete with a looping track and a giant microphone. The queue was long and clearly designed for adults. My father listened to a lot of rock music, so I recognized the style immediately.
RnR.3: That only added to the thrill, and roller coaster seats weren’t really designed for children back then. The safety bars were tight and uncomfortable. I often read online that people who were also around ten years old at the time remember this roller coaster vividly. Poor visibility, no idea what to expect, and then a sudden launch into a dark and the bumpy tunnel left a strong impression on all of us. It wasn't a fun beginner's roller coaster for kids that later turned out to be much less scary than expected. It was a way to grow bigger than you were. Growing bigger in a special way that would stay with you well into your years of a adult.

FreeFall.1: Another moment I will never forget is my first time in a Free Fall Tower. I was thirteen years old and at Movie Park with my parents. I heard my classmates talk about the Free Fall Towers and how cool they were. I really wanted to try it myself. Like many thirteen-year-olds, I wanted to look confident. I wore black leather Air Max shoes with shiny gold edges, rough jeans, and a worn-out polo shirt.
FreeFall.2: With full confidence, I said I wanted to try the High Fall first. But the higher we went, the faster my courage disappeared. When we reached sixty meters, I wished I had never stepped inside.
FreeFall.3: My brother stayed calm and said that sixty meters was not that high. I didn’t say anything back, because I didn’t want to look weak. It felt like we were turning around for hours before we finally reached the top. When the motor stopped, I could hear and feel my heartbeat. When the gondola dropped, I didn’t know what to feel. The fall was cold and intense.
FreeFall.4: My stomach made a turbo flight around the earth. I was too shocked to scream. When the gondola stopped suddenly, the excitement was complete. The feeling of relief and adrenaline made everything perfect. I had the best day of my life and felt big again.

autisme.1: I’ve always noticed that sensory input hits me harder than it does most people. Busy places and loud noises can quickly become overwhelming. That’s part of how autism works for me, and it’s something I sometimes have to take into account in daily life.
autisme.2:
That’s exactly why intense attractions have gained a special meaning for me. The first time I stepped into the Rock ’n’ Roller Coaster, I was completely overstimulated by the lights, the music, and the tension.

But the moment the launch started, something unexpected happened: all the scattered stimuli disappeared. There was only one thing left the experience itself.
autisme.3: In a roller coaster or drop tower, my attention is completely absorbed. As soon as I feel the tension building up, whether it’s waiting for the big drop on the High Fall or the first drop on a coaster, I feel completely free. Everything that normally feels like too much fades into the background for a moment.
autisme.4: It’s as if my mind goes completely quiet for a few seconds, while my body feels everything. That combination of focus, adrenaline, and freedom has only strengthened my love for intense sensations.

Europapark.1: My love for theme parks and roller coasters comes alive the most in Europa-Park. The park is big and has many different areas, but it still feels warm and friendly. The idea is simple: different parts of Europe are shown as themed areas, each with its own culture, atmosphere, and food, all inside a theme park.
Europapark.2: Europa‑Park is Germany’s largest theme park and one of the most beloved amusement parks in Europe. Located in Rust, near the French border, the park is known for its unique blend of themed areas, high‑quality attractions and warm, welcoming atmosphere. Each themed zone represents a different European country, complete with its own architecture, music and food.
Europapark.3: With more than one hundred attractions and shows including major roller coasters like Silver Star, Blue Fire and Voltron offers Europa‑Park something special for every type of visitor. From families with young children to dedicated thrillseekers, everyone can find a ride that matches their comfort level. The attention to detail, friendly staff and constant innovation make the park a place people love to return to.
Europapark.4: Europa-Park belongs to the Mack family, who are also known as the founders of the ride company Mack Rides. Because of this, the park feels not only like a place full of fun, but also like a show of their skill and work.

Autism and the Fairground.1: When people think of autism, they often imagine someone who cannot tolerate crowds, loud noises, or bright lights. At a fairground the music is loud, different sounds overlap, and there are lights everywhere.
Autism and the Fairground.2: Because of this, many assume that autistic people generally do not enjoy the fair unless the sensory‑friendly hour has started. Some autistic people do indeed avoid the fair entirely.
Autism and the Fairground.3: I am 2E (twice‑exceptional) myself, and I actually love the fair. The beat of the loud music combined with the warm atmosphere, the moving machines, the screams of the riders, and all the background sounds are calming for me rather than overwhelming.
Autism and the Fairground.4: I do wear mild sound dampeners. The same type you would use at a concert but they mainly help me avoid hearing everything at once rather than blocking out the sound.
Autism and the Fairground.5: My love for fairgrounds comes to life most strongly at the Tilburg Fair. The atmosphere in Tilburg feels unique, intense, pure, and complete to me. The selection of attractions is enormous: from an amazing view over the city in an 80‑meter free fall, where you plunge down screaming, to the madhouse full of funny obstacles and cheerful chaos.
Autism and the Fairground.6: Another thing I can completely absorbed in to is the sheer power of the ride Infinity. With your legs dangling freely in the air, fully letting go, and seeing the world upside down at 65 meters high—that feeling is unmatched for me.

Voltron.Info 1: Voltron takes you into a world of Tesla‑powered energy, where the track feels charged with electricity. Expect quick twists, sudden movements, and elements that appear almost out of nowhere like riding a bolt of lightning. It’s an adventure built around electric excitement, not just intensity. If you enjoy coasters that feel alive, coasters that twist, leap, and transform beneath you, Voltron delivers that feeling from start to finish.
Voltron.Info 2: A small tip: the queue is filled with powerful sound effects that build the atmosphere. If you’re sensitive to loud sounds, a pair of earplugs can make the wait more comfortable without taking away from the experience.
Voltron.trillvieuw: Voltron is fairly intense, especially for kids who are just above the height requirement. The launch, speed and rapid sequence of elements can feel overwhelming if this is your first major coaster. For beginners, it’s smart to ride Blue Fire and Wodan first. They help you understand speed, forces and inversions without the full intensity of Voltron. Make sure you’ve eaten enough, but not too much, both an empty and a heavy stomach can make the ride less comfortable. Young riders benefit from calm guidance: explain what will happen and stay reassuring until they board. The queue can be loud, so earplugs are useful.

Wodan.Info:
Wodan is a substantial wooden roller coaster.

The height restriction is low, but not for inexperienced riders.

The ride is powerful and thrilling, and the queue itself is an attraction, with a walkway past the most feared idols from Norse and Germanic mythology.
Wodan.trillvieuw: Wodan is a powerful wooden roller coaster with plenty of thrills. The height restriction of 120 cm is relatively low, but it is certainly not a junior coaster. The ride is quite intense. The seat cushions provide sufficient comfort and absorb some of the track's roughness. Eat normally, not too much and not too little. Let kids know that the shaking is normal and not a sign of anything being wrong. The queue is dark and atmospheric; staying in conversation can help younger riders feel secure.

Silverstar.Info:
With a top speed of 130 km/h, the Silverstar is the fastest and tallest roller coaster at Europa Park.

You can choose your seat on the Silverstar, so choose the front row for the best view and the most wind in your face for a greater sense of speed.

Choose the back row for more airtime. It's up to you and one more tip: swing your arms in the air for even more excitement and airtime.
Silverstar.trillvieuw: Silver Star is impressive mainly because of its height. The ride itself is smooth, but the open design and the view can feel overwhelming for first‑timers. If you’ve never ridden a major coaster before, start with Blue Fire. It gives you a solid foundation before tackling Silver Star’s scale. Eat lightly but sufficiently. For kids, reassure them that the height is safe and the restraints are secure. The queue is calm, but the top of the lift hill can be intense, prepare them for that moment..

Schweizer Bobbahn.Info: An old-fashioned bobsled run, of which there aren't many left. Fun for a change and not too extreme. The track is also beautifully designed to complement the Swiss theme area. The Schweizer Bobbahn is one of the few remaining operational bobsled coasters in theme parks. This makes the ride quite special, although it’s more of a family coaster than an intense thrill experience. It’s a fun change of pace, and the theming is nicely done. If you’re a true roller coaster enthusiast, it’s still worth checking off your list, since you won’t come across many rides like this in other parks.

Poseidon.Info:
Beautifully designed water coaster themed around Greek mythology.

It's a family-friendly and fun roller coaster with a splash that's not as big as Atlantica Super Splash.

Pegasus.Info: In an archaeological excavation area in the Greek themed section, the youngest visitors can experience their first roller coaster adventure.

Matterhorn Blitz.Info: A fun, classic Wild Mouse roller coaster themed around Switzerland. It's a good family coaster with excellent theming.

Euromir.Info: This is a classic spinning coaster with a catchy soundtrack. Depending on your position in the train, the coaster can be a bit taxing, especially if you start forward on the first drop and end up backward on the helix.
Euromir.trillvieuw: Euro Mir isn’t extreme, but the spinning cars and rhythmic motion can make some riders dizzy. If you get motion sick easily, ride Euro Mir after the other major coasters, not before. Eat lightly and stay hydrated.

Cancan coaster.Info:
The Eurosat - CanCan Coaster is a themed indoor roller coaster in the French themed area.

It is housed in a large geodesic dome and simulates a ride through Paris at night, featuring the atmosphere of the Moulin Rouge and CanCan dancers.

It also offers the option of a VR experience with a separate branch known as Eurosat Coastiality.

Blue Fire.Info 1: Blue Fire immerses you in an Icelandic research facility where strange energy pulses through volcanic rock. The preshow slowly builds the tension: flickering screens, rumbling effects and a train preparing for something powerful. As the doors open, you drift through rugged basalt formations — a calm introduction that gives you just enough time to realise something spectacular is coming.
Blue Fire.Info 2: Then comes the moment Blue Fire is famous for: the explosive launch that propels you from 0 to 100 km/h in just a few seconds. You burst into the open air and dive straight into the massive vertical loop, a smooth and iconic inversion that defines the ride. What follows is a mix of rapid turns, rock tunnels, a corkscrew and the signature heartline roll skimming just above the ground.
Blue Fire.Info 3: For thrillseekers, Blue Fire is pure joy — hands up, full speed, effortless flow. And if you’re lucky, the on‑ride camera will capture your entire adventure. Observant visitors can even find a small viewing hut near the launch, where you can watch the train through a window and see the nervous faces of riders just moments before they’re blasted into the sky.
Blue Fire.Info 4: Blue Fire blends theming, speed and smooth inversions into an experience that’s both welcoming for newcomers and exhilarating for those who crave a little extra adrenaline.
Blue Fire.trillvieuw: Blue Fire is an excellent first looping coaster. The launch is powerful but predictable, and the inversions are smooth and easy to follow. For kids experiencing their first upside‑down ride, this is the best option in the park. Explain that the restraint is tight on purpose and that feeling nervous before the launch is completely normal. Eat normally, not too heavy. The queue is calm and open, which helps reduce anxiety.
Blue Fire.video 2:
Blue Fire is a special coaster to me, which is why I created a personal tribute video. During my ride, the on‑ride camera captured my reaction, and I combined that footage with several external shots of the coaster in action.

The video shows riders reacting to the launch, the screams echoing through the massive loop and the smooth way the train twists through its roll elements. Together with my own on‑ride reaction, it captures exactly why Blue Fire is such a unique and unforgettable experience for me.

Ba-a-a Express.Info: Ba-a-a Express is a small junior coaster located in the farm-themed area. It’s designed for young children who want to try their very first roller coaster. For adults without kids, this ride isn’t particularly exciting, and in many cases you won’t be allowed to ride unless you’re accompanying a child. The layout is gentle, close to the ground, and mainly meant to help kids build confidence.

Atlantica Supersplash.Info: A nice water coaster with one steep drop and a big splash in the Portuguese theme area.

Arthur.Info: Arthur isn't a real roller coaster, but more of a dark ride. It's an adventure through the Kingdom of the Minimoys.

Alpen Express.Info: Alpen Express is a great family coaster.
